title: Which of the following statements about diagnoses is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A surgeon should always know the definitive diagnosis prior to performing any surgical procedure.
omfs: If a surgeon has no clue as to what a patient's diagnosis is, they should still perform a surgical procedure.
midterm: If a surgeon does not know the definitive diagnosis prior to performing a surgical procedure, they should develop a differential diagnosis including potential diagnoses.
column5: The same treatment should always be performed for the same diagnosis.
column6: A good surgeon can look at a pathologic lesion in a patient's mouth and know exactly what it is.

title: All of the following are reasons that a dentist may obtain an inaccurate history, EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The patient has low health literacy.
omfs: The patient may be able to realize secondary gain by withholding or providing inaccurate information.
midterm: The patient is withholding information that they may be embarrassed by because they feel the dentist does not need to know that information.
column5: The patient is a poor historian.
column6: The patient and dentist are not fluent in the same language.
column7: All of the above statements are reasons that a dentist may obtain an inaccurate history.

title: Consider the following two patients. F. 56 year-old female who had a hysterectomy 2 years ago and is hypothyroid following thyroidectomy for thyroid cancer. M. 56 year-old male who ran marathons up until 8 months ago when he had 2 stents placed when he had a heart attack. What ASA classification would you assign to each patient:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: F = ASA II and M = ASA III.
omfs: F = ASA III and M = ASA IV.
midterm: F = ASA III and M = ASA III.
column5: F = ASA IV and M = ASA IV.
column6: F = ASA III and M = ASA II.
column7: F = ASA II and M = ASA IV.

title: Which of the following statements about disturbances in hemostasis is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: If a patient has a significant bleeding episode following a surgical procedure, the surgeon did not necessarily make an error in judgement or technique.
omfs: NSAIDS may cause coagulation problems following a surgical procedure but acetaminophen will not.
midterm: Once a patient has been diagnosed with a hemophilia or quantitative platelet disorder, their bleeding risk remains constant, unless some corrective treatment is provided.
column5: DDAVP and corticosteroids can both be effective in elevating blood levels of a patient's coagulation factors and platelets.
column6: Medical personnel should always be suspicious that patients with prosthetic heart valves, atrial fibrillation, DVT's (deep vein thromboses), and PE's (pulmonary emboli), and patients following coronary artery stenting are anti-coagulated and thus have an increased bleeding risk.

title: Which of the following statements is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A patient on a target specific anticoagulant should have blood tests prior to a planned extraction to check if their INR is 2.5 or below and the extraction can be done.
omfs: A patient on a target specific anticoagulant should have blood tests prior to a planned extraction to check if their INR is 4.0 or below and the extraction can be done.
midterm: Although INR monitoring is mandatory for patients on target specific anticoagulants so that their medication dose can be adjusted as needed, this monitoring is often done at less frequent intervals than for patients on warfarin.
column5: The target INR for all patients is the same, even if they are being anticoagulated for different conditions.
column6: NONE of these statements is TRUE.

title: Which of the following statements about “bridging” is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: This technique is useful for minimizing the risk to a patient on warfarin if their anticoagulation needs to be interrupted for a procedure.
omfs: This technique involves stopping the patient's anticoagulation for 10 days both before and after the procedure.
midterm: This technique is useful for patients with a low clotting risk who will be undergoing a low bleeding risk procedure.
column5: During bridging, a patient should never be on two anticoagulants at the same time.
column6: An advantage of this technique is that no blood tests need to be performed.

title: Which of the following statements about vaso-vagal syncope is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Dental providers should be knowledgeable about the prevention of vaso-vagal syncope as this occurrence makes up approximately 50% of all medical emergencies that occur in the dental office.
omfs: When vaso-vagal syncope occurs, blood pressure decreases and heart rate increases.
midterm: Pre-operative hydration can be helpful in preventing vaso-vagal syncope.
column5: Supplemental oxygen delivery can be helpful in preventing vaso-vagal syncope.
column6: Physiological and psychologic factors can both contribute to the occurrence of vaso-vagal syncope.

title: Which of the following conditions does NOT put patients at increased risk of infection?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Hyperthyroidism.
omfs: Alcohol abuse.
midterm: End stage renal disease.
column5: Hematologic malignancies.
column6: Chemotherapy.

title: Which of the following statements about diabetic patients is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Compared to non-diabetic patients, both well-controlled and poorly-controlled diabetics have an increased risk of infection.
omfs: Compared to non-diabetic patients, infections are more difficult to control in both well-controlled and poorly-controlled diabetics.
midterm: Insulin doses should be adjusted based on pre-op intake for diabetics undergoing oral surgical procedures.
column5: Insulin doses should be adjusted based on anticipated post-op intake for diabetics undergoing oral surgical procedures.
column6: Mild-moderate hyperglycemia is preferred over hypoglycemia in diabetics in the peri-operative period.

title: Which of the following statements about antibiotic prophylaxis is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Bacteremia resulting from surgical manipulation during oral surgery can cause bacterial seeding of a damaged native or prosthetic valve resulting in subacute bacterial endocarditis.
omfs: If a patient already on antibiotics requires antibiotic prophylaxis prior to an oral surgical procedure, an antibiotic from another class should be used to reduce the risk from resistant organisms.
midterm: Prophylactic antibiotics are generally not recommended prior to oral surgical treatment to prevent prosthetic joint infection.
column5: Patients with immunocompromising medical conditions or joint replacement complications may require prophylactic antibiotics prior to oral surgical treatment to prevent prosthetic joint infection.
column6: None of these statements is FALSE.

title: Which of the following statements about adrenally suppressed patients is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Complex prolonged surgery may cause adrenal crisis in adrenally suppressed patients.
omfs: Adrenally suppressed patients undergoing most dental procedures do not require supplemental steroids.
midterm: If a surgical procedure requires steroid supplementation for a patient on steroids at the time of surgery, additional doses of steroids should be given on the day before surgery, the day of surgery, and the day following surgery.
column5: If a patient was on 10 mg or more of hydrocortisone for 1 week or more within the previous year and they are undergoing a procedure that would require steroid supplementation, steroids should be given in increasing doses for 2 weeks beginning the day before the surgery.
column6: If adrenal crisis develops in an adrenally suppressed patient, symptoms may include hypotension, increased pulse, syncope, nausea, and fever.

title: Which of the following is NOT a sign of a cerebrovascular accident?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Loss of balance, headache, or dizziness.
omfs: Blurred vision.
midterm: One side of the face is drooping.
column5: Arm or leg weakness.
column6: Speech difficulty.

title: Which of the following statements about treating infected teeth is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: If a dentoalveolar abscess arises from pulpal involvement of a tooth, the surgeon must wait for complete resolution of the infection prior to extracting the tooth.
omfs: The most rapid resolution of an acute dentoalveolar infection caused by pulpal involvement of a tooth will be achieved by extraction of that tooth.
midterm: Trismus from an infected tooth may complicate extraction of the tooth.
column5: Tooth related infection may make it more difficult to achieve adequate local anesthesia for extraction.
column6: Extraction of an impacted third molar in the presence of severe pericoronitis is accompanied by an increased incidence of complications.

title: Consider the following radiographs showing primary teeth requiring extraction. Which accompanying statement is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The mandibular left primary second molar seen in this radiograph may be difficult to extract because it is submerged and potentially ankylosed.
omfs: The mandibular right primary second molar seen in this periapical radiograph may be difficult to extract because it has been root canal treated, has a large restoration, and has not had any resorption of its roots.
midterm: The mandibular left primary first and second molars seen in this periapical radiograph should be easy to extract because the roots appear to be significantly resorbed.
column5: The mandibular right primary second molar seen in this periapical radiograph may be difficult to extract because the mesial root is thin and has not had any resorption of its length.
column6: The mandibular right primary second molar seen in this periapical radiograph may be difficult to extract because it has widespread roots and if extraction necessitates sectioning of the tooth, the succedaneous premolar tooth bud is at risk of being damaged.

title: Consider the periapical radiographs below and the statements that follow: EXTERNAL RESORPTION INTERNAL RESORPTION Statement I: Extraction of the tooth undergoing external resorption may be difficult as the tooth may be prone to fracture. Statement II: Extraction of the tooth undergoing internal resorption may be difficult as the tooth may be prone to fracture. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Only I is TRUE.
omfs: Only II is TRUE.
midterm: I and II are both TRUE.
column5: I and II are both FALSE.

title: You are extracting a mandibular second premolar. You have achieved adequate mobility of the tooth with a straight elevator. You are now using a 151 forceps but cannot complete the extraction because the beaks keep sliding around on the tooth. Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: You are using a forceps designed for maxillary teeth and should switch to a 150 forceps which, unlike the 151 forceps, is designed for extracting mandibular teeth.
omfs: An Ash forceps may be more effective as the beaks may grasp the tooth more effectively.
midterm: Adjusting the beaks of the forceps so that they are seated as apically as possible may be helpful.
column5: Adjusting the beaks of the forceps so that they are better seated along the long axis of the tooth may be helpful.
column6: All of these strategies may be helpful.

title: Consider the following statements: I. Tooth and/or bone fragments or debris left at the surgical site may result in post-operative infection. II. Surgical handpieces blow air into the surgical field to clear the field of tooth and/ or bone fragments and debris that result from drilling into teeth or bone. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Only I is TRUE.
omfs: Only II is TRUE.
midterm: I and II are both TRUE.
column5: I and II are both FALSE.

title: Which of the following statements describing the use of a scalpel to make an incision is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: When making an incision with a scalpel, mobile tissues should be stabilized.
omfs: The mucosa, submucosal tissues, and periosteum should each be incised in a separate cutting motion.
midterm: A “pen grasp” should be used to maintain maximum control.
column5: A “15 blade” is most commonly used for oral surgical procedures.
column6: None of these statements are FALSE.

title: Which of the following instruments CANNOT be used for bone removal?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Surgical handpiece and bur.
omfs: Rongeur.
midterm: Chisel.
column5: Bone file.
column6: All of these instruments can be used for bone removal.

title: Which of the following statements about the use of straight elevators is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Forceful movements are required to achieve adequate mobility of a tooth.
omfs: The convex surface of the elevator should be applied to the tooth being extracted.
midterm: They can only be used when adjacent teeth are present to manipulate against.
column5: A “pen grasp” should be used to apply maximum force.
column6: None of these statements is TRUE.

title: Which of the following statements about the use of periotomes for extractions is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: They may be advantageous for preserving socket anatomy when performing extractions.
omfs: They are used to sever PDL fibers.
midterm: They are only used effectively in the first 2 - 3 mm of the PDL space.
column5: They are used by applying apically directed pressure circumferentially around the tooth
column6: Eventual delivery of the tooth is accomplished with forceps.

title: “Surgical” or “open” extraction technique is indicated for all of the following EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: When excess force would otherwise be necessary.
omfs: When a substantial portion of the crown is missing or covered by tissue.
midterm: When access to the root or fragment of the root is difficult or limited.
column5: When closed technique would pose additional risk to vital structures.
column6: When the tooth to be extracted has advanced periodontal disease.

title: All of the following are useful techniques for performing extractions, EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: When extracting mandibular teeth, the jaw should be supported by having the patient bite on a bite block.
omfs: When extracting maxillary teeth, the jaw should be supported by the operator or assistant pushing up on the patient's chin.
midterm: The operator's non-dominant hand and/or fingers can be useful for retracting.
column5: The operator's non-dominant hand and/or fingers can be useful for tactile purposes such as determining if inadvertent mobilization of an adjacent tooth or restoration is occurring.
column6: The operator's non-dominant hand and/or fingers can be useful for controlling tooth/restoration fragments that may fracture off during an extraction.

title: Which of the following statements regarding the effects of tooth-specific factors on difficulty of extraction is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Extraction of maxillary lateral incisors may be complicated by distal curvature of the root.
omfs: Maxillary second premolars and single rooted first premolars generally have conical roots, making them amenable to extraction by rotational movements.
midterm: Extraction of maxillary second molars is generally easier than extraction of maxillary first molars because their roots are generally shorter and less divergent, and their buccal roots are often fused.
column5: Although mandibular premolars often have conical roots making them amenable to extraction by rotation, extraction may be made more difficult due to roots that are curved or have bulbous apices.
column6: Extraction of mandibular second molars may be more difficult than extraction of mandibular first molars because they generally have roots that are more widely divergent.

title: Which of the following statements about extractions is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The treatment plan for subsequent tooth replacement should be considered when determining the extraction technique to be used.
omfs: Surgical extraction techniques generally provide greater access to safely remove a tooth or root.
midterm: Surgical extraction techniques do not allow for contouring or smoothing of bone at the time of extraction.
column5: Compared to surgical extraction techniques, closed extraction techniques may be more traumatic or morbid, resulting in a greater likelihood of unintended crown or root fracture.
column6: Compared to surgical extraction techniques, closed extraction techniques may be more traumatic or morbid, with an increased risk of sinus exposure when extracting maxillary posterior teeth.

title: Which of the following statements regarding surgical flaps is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: When designing a flap, the base should be broader than free margin, allowing for an adequate blood supply to prevent ischemic necrosis of the flap.
omfs: Periosteum should be preserved as it is the primary tissue responsible for bone healing.
midterm: Improper placement of an incision can result in wound dehiscence and delayed healing.
column5: Incisions in the retromolar region of the mandible should be flared to the buccal to minimize the risk of damaging the lingual nerve.
column6: Releasing incisions carry a much higher risk of complications at the anterior palatine foramen region when compared to the greater palatine foramen region.

title: Which of the following statements about elevating a flap is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: A sharp scalpel blade should be used when making an incision.
omfs: The spearpoint end of the periosteal elevator should be used to elevate the flap.
midterm: When elevating a flap, it is most effective and least damaging to the papilla to elevate from the angled length of the papilla rather than from the apex of the papilla.
column5: Injecting local anesthesia under the periosteum will make it more difficult to elevate a full thickness mucoperiosteal flap.
column6: A retractor should be positioned to rest on bone without placing tension on the soft tissues.

title: Which of the following statements about surgical extractions is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: The beaks of an extraction forceps should never be placed on the bone overlying a root to be extracted.
omfs: If limited access is preventing extraction of a fractured root, elevation of a flap may enable extraction by allowing for adequate positioning of an elevator and/or forceps, even without removing bone.
midterm: Once an extraction is begun, all root fragments should be removed, no matter how much bone needs to be removed to accomplish their removal.
column5: After completing an open extraction, the operator should directly palpate the exposed bony edges and aggressively smooth any sharp areas.
column6: Irrigation prior to closing a flap is only necessary if there may be tooth fragments or debris under the flap as they may result in post-operative infection. Bone fragments or debris cannot result in post-operative infection.

title: Consider the following statements about bone removal during surgical extractions: I. When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth for extraction, it is important to preserve the buccal and lingual/palatal cortical plates. II. When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth for extraction, it is important to preserve the interseptal bone - the bone between the tooth being extracted and the adjacent teeth). III. When sectioning a multi-rooted tooth for extraction, it is important to preserve the interradicular bone - the bone between the individual roots of the tooth being extracted. Which of the following is correct:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Only I is TRUE.
omfs: Only II is TRUE.
midterm: Only III is TRUE.
column5: Only I and II are TRUE.
column6: Only I and III are TRUE.
column7: Only II and III are TRUE.
column8: I, II, and III are TRUE.

title: Hard and soft tissue surgical procedures are often necessary prior to designing and fabricating prostheses for patients. All of the following are necessary when evaluating a patient for a prosthesis EXCEPT:
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Assessment of interarch relationships.
omfs: Assessment of skeletal relationships.
midterm: Radiograph examination for the presence of impacted teeth, retained roots, and pathology.
column5: Radiograph examination for the location of the mental and lingual nerves.
column6: Visual examination and palpation for bony undercuts, protuberances, tori, exostoses, post-tuberosity notching, height of palatal vault, and depth of vestibules.

title: Which of the following statements about INTRASEPTAL ALVEOPLASTY is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: This procedure is indicated when contouring of irregularities of the buccal bone is necessary.
omfs: This procedure results in decreased alveolar ridge thickness.
midterm: This procedure maintains alveolar ridge height.
column5: This procedure is useful for the reduction or elimination of buccal undercuts.
column6: This procedure involves the use of a rongeur and/or a surgical handpiece and bur for cutting intraseptal bone.

title: Which of the following statements about pre-prosthetic surgery is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: Maxillary torus reduction may be made more difficult because the overlying mucosa may be thin and extend into the invaginations between the lobes of the torus.
omfs: Mandibular torus reduction may be made more difficult because the overlying mucosa may be thin and extend into the invaginations between the lobes of the torus.
midterm: In some cases maxillary or mandibular torus reduction may be effectively accomplished by reduction of excess soft tissue only.
column5: Infection may result from displacement of bone fragments or debris into the floor of the mouth during mandibular torus reduction.
column6: Oro-nasal communication may result as a complication of maxillary tuberosity reduction.

title: Which of the following statements is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: When performing soft tissue pre-prosthetic procedures, the operator must be aware that their choice of technique may cause a reduction in vestibular depth.
omfs: When performing pre-prosthetic procedures, the operator must be aware that the location where the inferior alveolar nerve exits the mandible may have been altered due to resorption of the mandible.
midterm: When performing soft tissue pre-prosthetic procedures, the operator should use a technique that achieves healing by primary intention to achieve the optimal result while promoting the quickest healing and most comfortable post-operative recovery.
column5: When incising the frenum along the base of the tongue during a lingual frenectomy, the operator should cut along a clamp as this helps to avoid cutting into the floor of the mouth and aids in hemostasis.
column6: When removing an epulis, the operator may use different techniques based on the amount of tissue that needs to be removed.

title: Which of the following statements about the transpositional flap vestibuloplasty is TRUE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: All incisions should be made to develop full thickness mucoperiosteal flaps.
omfs: The height of the bone does not matter as this is a soft tissue procedure intended to increase the facial vestibular depth.
midterm: The lingual vestibular depth does not matter as this procedure is intended to increase the facial vestibular depth.
column5: This procedure yields reliable predictable results.
column6: This procedure does not involve placement of a skin graft.

title: Which of the following statements about the submucosal vestibuloplasty for maxillary ridge extension is FALSE?
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: This procedure is used to achieve better stability and retention of maxillary dentures.
omfs: Adequate pre-operative evaluation must be performed to avoid esthetic changes such as shortening or inversion of the upper lip.
midterm: A splint is used to hold the mucosa against the periosteum at the depth of vestibule until healing has occurred.
column5: Submucosal and supraperiosteal tunneling is performed so that tissues can be effectively repositioned without the actual excision of any tissue.
column6: An anterior vertical incision is used to allow entry for submucosal and supraperiosteal tunneling.

title: BONUS: A throat screen should be used to minimize the risk of aspiration or ingestion of objects such as teeth, restorations, small instruments and other objects.
Oral & Maxillofacial Surgery Midterm Exa: True
omfs: False
